The second pathway connects Paeonilactone C to Asialoglycoprotein receptor 2, which is targeted by (+)-Actinidine, which in turn targets Retinoic acid receptor alpha. These findings indicate that Paeonilactone C may act as a modulator of Retinoic acid receptor alpha through different molecular mechanisms, possibly by influencing the expression or activity of downstream targets. The evidence is consistent with the possibility that Paeonilactone C exerts its biological effects through these indirect pathways, though the exact mechanism of interaction remains to be elucidated.
